title: Function-call JSON parameter surface and friendly fault protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:

We need a pragmatic, forward-compatible JSON schema profile for function/tool parameters that balances strict validation during onboarding with forgiving runtime behavior for production calls. This ticket proposes a surface for authoring parameter schemas, the runtime validation modes, and a developer-friendly error protocol (error codes, remediation hints, and telemetry buckets). The goal is to reduce customer confusion from opaque schema failures, provide automated remediation hints, and enable graceful compatibility with older SDK/tool manifests.

Context & motivation:
- Customers submit function/tool manifests to Redwood via the API or Console. Current failures are often cryptic (e.g. stack traces or "invalid params"), increasing support load.
- We want to adopt a consistent schema grammar that supports: typed fields, coercion hints, enumerations, size constraints, and deprecation metadata.
- Runtime must support two validation modes: "soft" (best-effort/coerce + nonblocking telemetry) and "strict" (reject calls with explicit error codes). Soft mode improves forward compatibility for third-party callers; strict mode is required for high-sensitivity customers (enterprise, Private).

Proposal (high level):
1) Schema authoring surface: a compact JSON profile inspired by JSON Schema but with a smaller, opinionated subset (types: string, number, integer, boolean, object, array; annotations: required, enum, maxLength, min, max, pattern, deprecated, default, coerce). Authors may include a short "help" string for user-visible messages.
2) Validation modes: "strict" | "soft". Default: "soft" for hosted API. Private/Dedicated customers may opt-in to strict. Soft mode attempts coercion in this order: string->number (if numeric), string->boolean ("true"/"false"), array coercion for single-item values, and trimming for strings. Coercion that succeeds is recorded in telemetry.
3) Error protocol: machine-readable error object with fields: code, path, message, hint, suggested_fix. Error codes we will introduce: ERR_PARAM_REQUIRED, ERR_PARAM_TYPE, ERR_PARAM_COERCE_FAILED, ERR_PARAM_UNKNOWN_FIELD, ERR_PARAM_TOO_LONG, ERR_PARAM_OUT_OF_RANGE, ERR_PARAM_DEPRECATED. Hints and suggested_fix are short developer-facing strings to be surfaced in our SDKs/console.
4) Compatibility shim: runtime will accept older manifest shapes by running a one-time schema normalization pass (legacy key mapping table) and annotating normalized fields with provenance metadata. Customers will see a migration warning in Console and an opt-in flag to enforce strictness post-migration.

Operational notes:
- Telemetry: emit param_error_bucket with tags {code, validation_mode, model_shard, route, customer_tier}. Record whether coercion was applied and original value (masked for PII).
- Observability: Console will expose a per-route validation dashboard with common failing paths and top suggested fixes.
- DevX: SDKs should include: friendly exception mapping (human_message), auto-coercion toggle, and a linting tool to validate manifests locally before upload.

Acceptance criteria (see field below):
- Authoring doc published + example gallery
- Runtime implements soft + strict validation mode and emits telemetry
- SDKs map machine errors to human messages and show suggested_fix when available

Notes on trade-offs:
- We limit schema features to avoid complexity (no full-of-rules JSON Schema superset). This reduces expressivity but improves implementation safety across runtimes (Go, Rust, Python).
- Coercion is intentionally lossy in soft mode; we record coercion so customers can tighten to strict later.
acceptance_criteria: Authoring guide and examples published in Confluence
Runtime supports 'soft' and 'strict' validation modes across hosted and private deployments
Server emits param_error_bucket telemetry for all validation failures and coercions
Console shows per-route validation summary and top 10 failing parameter paths
SDKs convert machine errors to user-friendly messages and surface suggested_fix
